def solve_tsp(distance_matrix: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:

    if n <= 3:
        tour = np.arange(n)
        report_best_tour(tour)
        return tour

    remaining = set(range(3, n))

        before = tour[pos-1]
        after = tour[pos] if pos < len(tour) else tour[0]
        return distance_matrix[before, city] + distance_matrix[city, after] - distance_matrix[before, after]
    # insert all remaining

        best_city = -1
        best_regret = -1
        best_pos = -1

                    new_tour[i+1:j+1] = reversed(tour[i+1:j+1])

import numpy as np

def solve_tsp(distance_matrix: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    n = distance_matrix.shape[0]
    if n == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=np.int64)
    if n == 1:
        return np.array([0], dtype=np.int64)
    
    best_tour = None
    best_cost = np.inf
    
    # Randomized greedy construction with RCL (size = max(2, int(sqrt(n))))
    rcl_size = max(2, int(np.sqrt(n)))
    
    for _ in range(1):  # single run; could be extended
        start = np.random.randint(n)
        tour = [start]
        unvisited = set(range(n))
        unvisited.remove(start)
        current = start
        while unvisited:
            # compute distances to unvisited
            dists = distance_matrix[current, list(unvisited)]
            # sort indices by distance
            sorted_indices = np.argsort(dists)
            sorted_cities = np.array(list(unvisited))[sorted_indices]
            # choose randomly from first rcl_size
            k = min(rcl_size, len(sorted_cities))
            candidate = sorted_cities[np.random.randint(k)]
            tour.append(candidate)
            unvisited.remove(candidate)
            current = candidate
        tour = np.array(tour, dtype=np.int64)
        # 2-opt improvement
        improved = True
        while improved:
            improved = False
            for i in range(n - 1):
                for j in range(i + 2, n):
                    # if j == i+1, skip (adjacent edges)
                    if j == i + 1:
                        continue
                    # compute delta
                    a, b, c, d = tour[i], tour[(i+1)%n], tour[j], tour[(j+1)%n]
                    old = distance_matrix[a, b] + distance_matrix[c, d]
                    new = distance_matrix[a, c] + distance_matrix[b, d]

import numpy as np

def solve_tsp(distance_matrix: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    n = len(distance_matrix)
    if n <= 2:
        tour = np.arange(n)
        report_best_tour(tour.copy())
        return tour
    # find two farthest cities
    max_dist = 0
    start = end = 0
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i+1, n):
            d = distance_matrix[i, j]
            if d > max_dist:
                max_dist = d
                start, end = i, j
    tour = [start, end]
    remaining = set(range(n)) - {start, end}
    while remaining:
        # find farthest node from current tour
        farthest_dist = -1
        farthest_node = None
        for node in remaining:
            min_dist = min(distance_matrix[node, t] for t in tour)
            if min_dist > farthest_dist:
                farthest_dist = min_dist
                farthest_node = node
        # find best insertion position
        best_increase = float('inf')
        best_pos = 0
        for i in range(len(tour)):
            prev = tour[i]
            nxt = tour[(i+1) % len(tour)]
            increase = distance_matrix[prev, farthest_node] + distance_matrix[farthest_node, nxt] - distance_matrix[prev, nxt]
            if increase < best_increase:
                best_increase = increase
                best_pos = i+1
        tour.insert(best_pos, farthest_node)
        remaining.remove(farthest_node)
    tour_arr = np.array(tour)
    report_best_tour(tour_arr)
    # 2-opt improvement
    improved = True
    while improved:
        improved = False
        for i in range(n-1):
            for j in range(i+2, n):
                if j-i == 1:
                    continue
                # consider reversal of segment i+1..j
                i1 = i
                i2 = i+1
                j1 = j
                j2 = (j+1) % n
                if distance_matrix[tour[i1], tour[i2]] + distance_matrix[tour[j1], tour[j2]] > distance_matrix[tour[i1], tour[j1]] + distance_matrix[tour[i2], tour[j2]]:

                    tour = tour[:i+1] + tour[i+1:j+1][::-1] + tour[j+1:]
